`config show`'s git.origin is the NORMALIZED locator rung 4 matches, not the raw remote URL a reader could already get from git (2phzt)

`config show` prints its evidence to stdout even when the resolution refuses, so an origin two projects claim — the question the verb exists to answer — is diagnosable rather than a bare exit 5 (2phzt)

The Git facts `config show` reports describe the directory, not the scope: --inbox names a project without consulting the ladder, and reporting no git.root would say "not in a repository" of a checkout (2phzt)

-a widens an id completion to closed issues, the same flag that widens list (zwuh8)
reopen is the one exception to the live default: it completes closed issues, because a live-only list offers nothing it can act on (zwuh8)
list and count's --status completion offers the literal "all" widening value; update's single status does not (zwuh8)
-P/--project completes every slug, archived included, because -P still scopes to an archived project's history (zwuh8)
move --to completes only live slugs, because an archived project is never a legal destination (zwuh8)
-l completes the labels that already exist in the selected scope, not an empty or store-wide guess (zwuh8)
